title: Design System: Imperial Street Auto Repair

display.purpose: Section headings (h2). Big Shoulders Display 800, uppercase, tight leading 0.92.

headline.purpose: Page title only (h1). Intentionally oversized at large viewports — industrial oversized-headline tradition. Uppercase always.

title.purpose: Card headings, component titles, h3. Manrope 700 — readable hierarchy, not industrial signage.

body.purpose: All running copy. Manrope 400-500. Max 65-75ch line length.

label.purpose: Kicker lines, phone numbers, technical metadata, pricing footnotes, navigation timestamps. JetBrains Mono — the precision-data register.

shadows.name: subtle-rule
shadows.purpose: Ambient separation. Elements that need to read above their background without announcing themselves.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover or floating card state. Appears only on :hover — cards are flat at rest.

shadows.name: table-structural
shadows.purpose: Services table only. A structural shadow that roots the full-width grid.

shadows.name: nav-scrolled
shadows.purpose: Sticky nav after scroll begins. Before scroll: no shadow, only the glassmorphic blur.

motion.name: ease-ui
motion.purpose: Default UI transitions: buttons, links, hover states.

motion.name: ease-card
motion.purpose: Card hover, nav link underline, status dot transitions.

motion.name: ease-carousel
motion.purpose: Shop photo carousel slide transition. Decelerate-into-stop — no bounce.

motion.name: ease-car-arrive
motion.purpose: Hero car cut-out entrance. One-shot on page load.

breakpoints.name: mobile-md
breakpoints.notes: Pricing grid, mobile pricing font sizes

breakpoints.name: mobile-lg
breakpoints.notes: Trust grid, process steps, reviews collapse to 1-col; FAB shows

breakpoints.name: tablet-lg
breakpoints.notes: Nav collapses to hamburger, why-grid to 2-col

narrative.overview:
Imperial Street Auto Repair's visual language is drawn from the aesthetic of a professional service manual — the kind of Bosch or Haynes technical reference that mechanics actually use. Compressed industrial type, structured information hierarchies, and a palette that says 'we have been doing this for fifteen years and we know what we are doing.' The design is confident without showmanship, precise without coldness.

The palette is a committed range of steel-blue tones stepped across sections — not a neutral background colour but the brand's own atmospheric hue. Deep corporate navy anchors structural elements. Electric blue fires as the sole accent: call-to-action buttons, kicker lines, the glow on active states. Mono type appears on labels, phone numbers, and data — not as a developer aesthetic but as precision-instrument reading, like the markings on a diagnostic gauge.

This system explicitly rejects the franchise auto-chain aesthetic, the greasy-garage cliché, and the cold SaaS dark-dashboard look. It also rejects the cream/warm-neutral landing-page default: the background is blue, not beige.
keyCharacteristics: Industrial compressed display type (Big Shoulders Display) — uppercase, tight leading, significant negative letter-spacing
Steel-blue tonal sections stepping through a single hue family to create section rhythm without changing the palette
Electric blue as the one accent colour: rare and purposeful, never decorative
Mono type for all data-adjacent labels: kickers, phone numbers, timestamps, pricing metadata
Near-square button corners (2px radius) matching the architectural, no-nonsense personality
Glassmorphic nav: the one justified use of blur in the system — separates structure from content without an opaque band

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Electric blue (#1f53d6) appears on ≤15% of any given section's surface. Its rarity creates the hierarchy. When everything is blue, nothing is.

rules.name: The Tonal Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Section backgrounds step through the steel-blue ramp, not alternate between unrelated hues. Every background colour on the page is a tint of the same family. New sections must use a value from the ramp, never an outside hue.

rules.name: The On-Dark Swap Rule
rules.body: On navy backgrounds, accent becomes --brass (#5d8df7), not the full electric blue. Full electric blue on navy lacks sufficient contrast; the lighter value reads clearly and still feels active.

rules.name: The Uppercase Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders Display appears uppercase only. It is a display face, not a body face. Sentences in Big Shoulders at normal weight and mixed case lose their industrial character and read as a wrong font choice.

rules.name: The Mono Precision Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono earns its place by context, not decoration. Use it for: phone numbers, technical kicker labels, category counters, timestamp metadata. Do not use it for body copy, navigation links, or headings.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards and pricing panels are flat at rest. The shadow appears only on :hover with a translateY(-2px) micro-lift. A resting shadow reads as the whole page floating; that is not the intent.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Before reaching for a shadow to create separation, reach for a background colour step. The section rhythm exists so that borders and shadows are not needed between sections.

dos: Do use Big Shoulders Display at 800+ weight, uppercase, with tight leading (0.88–0.92) for all h1 and h2 headings.
Do use electric blue (#1f53d6) sparingly — on CTAs, kicker accents, and active states only.
Do step through the steel-blue tonal ramp for section backgrounds. New sections must use a value from the #9bbae8–#c2d6f5 family.
Do use border-radius: 2px on buttons and sharp UI elements.
Do use JetBrains Mono for precision-data contexts: kicker labels, phone numbers, pricing metadata.
Do place the phone number (604) 434-1120 within reach on every section.
Do keep body copy at a maximum of 65–75ch line length.
Do ensure dark-section text (rgba(255,255,255,.78) or higher) maintains ≥4.5:1 contrast against the navy background.
donts: Don't use warm-neutral backgrounds (cream, sand, beige, paper). The body background is steel blue.
Don't make the site look like a franchise chain (Jiffy Lube, Midas) — no red/white corporate palette, no template-feel card grids.
Don't use the greasy-garage aesthetic — clip-art wrenches, racing stripes, checkered flags.
Don't drift into SaaS/startup territory — gradient hero backgrounds with floating blobs, big-number metric strips, glassmorphism everywhere.
Don't use JetBrains Mono for navigation links, headings, or body paragraphs.
Don't add rounded corners larger than 10px to structural containers.
Don't add an eyebrow/kicker label above every new section heading by reflex.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px as a colour accent) on cards, alerts, or callouts.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). All text is solid colour.
Don't add a second accent colour. One hue family, one accent.
